title: AI Safety, Robustness, and Generative Controls
summary: Specify the boundaries an assurance case must record for certified and empirical robustness evidence.

sections: AI Safety, Robustness, and Generative Controls

blocks.md:
By the end of this lesson you should be able to:

- Specify the boundaries an assurance case must record for certified and empirical robustness evidence
- Design fallback and abstention mechanisms under tight real-time latency budgets
- Classify and sequence the stages of the RLHF alignment pipeline
- Design safety and alignment guardrails for Retrieval-Augmented Generation architectures
- Analyze how Goodhart's law drives proxy metric misalignment in recommender systems

blocks.source: Vol II, Responsible AI, § AI Safety, Robustness, and Generative Controls
blocks.md: A model that withstands every tested perturbation can still cause harm when the operating environment leaves its validated envelope or when its objective rewards the wrong behavior. Safety governance therefore spans robustness claims bounded by a threat model, control surfaces for generative systems whose outputs cannot be enumerated in advance, and the alignment of the objective itself as systems act with greater autonomy.

blocks.title: What the section covers
blocks.md:
In the book this section runs through:

- Safety and robustness
- Generative control surfaces
- AI safety and value alignment
- Autonomous systems and trust
- Safety at fleet scale

Pay attention to: Certified versus empirical robustness evidence; Abstention and fallback latency budgets; Generative control surfaces (RLHF pipeline, alignment tax, RAG context filtering); Reward hacking, specification gaming, and proxy misalignment.

blocks.prompt: Think first: In high-speed autonomous control loops (e.g., drone navigation or collision avoidance), explain why implementing prediction abstention creates an immediate latency-budget challenge.
blocks.md: Abstention shifts the immediate decision to a fallback that must meet the physical hazard deadline. A validated local maneuver may act within milliseconds while human review follows on a longer timescale. Human takeover is a suitable immediate fallback only when a ready operator has enough time to act; referral alone does not satisfy the control deadline.

questions.q: A robustness report for a deployed model includes a randomized-smoothing certificate and an empirical attack evaluation. What must the assurance case record about each before a launch authority relies on it?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D. A certificate proves a property only for its stated norm, radius, confidence, and model configuration, and an empirical evaluation reports resistance only under the tested attack protocol. Neither establishes safety for the complete workflow, so governance records those boundaries to keep a narrow result from being promoted into a general safety claim.
questions.hint: Think about: specify the boundaries an assurance case must record for certified and empirical robustness evidence.
options: Nothing beyond the headline accuracy, because both results already establish that the end-to-end workflow is safe
Only the empirical result, because a certificate is a mathematical proof and needs no stated scope
Only the certificate, because empirical attack results guarantee immunity against all unseen attacks
The certificate's norm, radius, confidence, and model configuration, and the empirical evaluation's attack protocol, since each supports a claim only within those stated boundaries

questions.q: Order the 6 stages of the canonical Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) alignment pipeline from initial training to deployment:
questions.explanation: The correct order is (3) Base model pretraining on massive web-scale corpora, (1) Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) on curated instruction demonstrations, (5) Human rater pairwise preference data collection, (6) Reward Model training on preference comparisons, (2) Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) fine-tuning of the policy against the reward model, (4) Aligned model safety validation and deployment. The pipeline progresses from unsupervised foundation pretraining to supervised task tuning, preference modeling, reinforcement learning policy alignment, and final deployment gating.

items: Base model pretraining on massive web-scale corpora
Human rater pairwise preference data collection
Reward Model training on preference comparisons.

blocks.prompt: Explain it: In Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), why does RLHF of the core LLM fail to establish safety for the complete service, and what retrieval-path controls should be evaluated?
blocks.md: Retrieved material can influence answers outside the conditions covered by the core model's alignment evaluations. A biased retrieval index is one possible source of harmful output, not proof that the model must reproduce every document. Evaluate source selection, retrieval quality, context filtering, or output checks for the intended use; filtering alone does not establish absence of bias or harmful responses.

blocks.prompt: Explain it: Explain Goodhart's law in the context of production recommendation algorithms and describe how optimizing for Click-Through Rate (CTR) can create value misalignment.
blocks.md: Goodhart's law warns that optimizing a proxy can weaken its connection to the intended goal. A CTR objective may reward clickbait or other behavior that increases clicks without improving long-term welfare. Establishing that failure in production requires evidence about the policy's effects and the welfare criterion; choosing CTR alone does not prove harmful behavior.
